title: Etale direct image is exact for integral morphisms
statement:
Let $\pi:T'\to T$ be an
integral morphism of
schemes. Then the
direct image
$\pi_*:\Ab(T'_{\Et})\to\Ab(T_{\Et})$ is exact; consequently
$R^q\pi_*=0$ for $q>0$ and $R\pi_*=\pi_*$ on $\Dplus(T'_{\Et})$. If
$\pi$ is finite, this is [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]
of the proper-base-change chapter.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.43.5,
[Tag `04C2`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04C2).*)

proof.text: Let $\varphi:F\to G$ be an epimorphism of abelian sheaves on $T'_{\Et}$ and let $V\to T$ be etale with $s\in(\pi_*G)(V)=G(T'\times_TV)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], choose an etale covering $\{U_i\to T'\times_TV\}$ and sections $t_i\in F(U_i)$ whose images are $s|_{U_i}$. This applies to the small etale site of $T'$: the covering maps compose with the etale projection $T'\times_TV\to T'$ to give objects of that site. The composition is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], clause (2).

source.place: Tag 04C2 (lemma-what-integral), proof of (1) and (4), via Tags 04DR and 04DO

proof.text: For each point $v\in V$, apply [lem-sbc-integral-etale-cover-disjoint-refinement] with $f=\pi$ to this covering. It gives an etale neighbourhood $a_v:V_v\to V$ with a point above $v$, and a partition of $T'\times_TV_v$ into disjoint opens $W_{v,j}$, each mapping over $T'\times_TV$ to some $U_{\alpha_v(j)}$. Pull back $t_{\alpha_v(j)}$ to a section $r_{v,j}\in F(W_{v,j})$. Naturality of $\varphi$ gives $\varphi(r_{v,j})=s|_{W_{v,j}}$. The refinement lemma requires only that $\pi$ be integral, not finite or surjective. The opens are etale over the source, and their maps to the covering members are morphisms of its small etale site, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], clauses (1) and (2).

source.place: Tag 04C2 (lemma-what-integral), proof of (1) and (4), via Tags 04DR and 04DO

proof.text: The inclusions of the disjoint opens $W_{v,j}$ are monomorphisms and jointly cover $T'\times_TV_v$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-disjoint-etale-sections-product] to $F$ and $G$ on the small etale site of $T'$ (the products of abelian groups exist, also for an empty family). The tuple $(r_{v,j})_j$ glues uniquely to $r_v\in F(T'\times_TV_v)$, and the equality of the restrictions of $\varphi(r_v)$ and $s|_{T'\times_TV_v}$ forces equality of those sections. Thus $s|_{V_v}$ lifts in $(\pi_*F)(V_v)$. The family $\{V_v\to V\}_{v\in V}$ is etale and jointly surjective because its $v$-indexed member has a point over $v$; it is a covering. The local-surjectivity criterion on $T_{\Et}$ now proves that $\pi_*\varphi$ is an epimorphism. If $V$ is empty, the empty covering gives the same criterion. The open inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], clause (1); the base neighbourhoods are objects over $T$ by clause (2).

proof.text: For every short exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$, [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-left-exact] gives exactness of $0\to\pi_*F_1\to\pi_*F_2\to\pi_*F_3$; the epimorphism preservation just proved supplies its last surjection. Therefore the additive functor $\pi_*$ carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences, which is exactness.

source.place: Tag 04C2 (lemma-what-integral), proof of (1) and (4), via Tags 04DR and 04DO

proof.text: The categories of abelian etale sheaves on $T'$ and $T$ have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-sc-exact-functor-higher-derived-vanishing] to the exact additive functor $\pi_*$ obtained above. It gives $R^q\pi_*(F)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $F$ and every integer $q>0$, hence the asserted vanishing of functors.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to $\pi_*$: the termwise functor carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and induces a derived functor. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] it restricts to the bounded below categories. Now [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], clause (2), identifies this restriction canonically with the right derived functor $R\pi_*$: for every bounded below complex $K$ the canonical map $Q(\pi_*K)\to R\pi_*(QK)$ is an isomorphism. This is precisely $R\pi_*=\pi_*$ on $\Dplus(T'_{\Et})$, with the right side understood termwise on complexes.

tool_uses.why: The small-etale local lifting criterion converts epimorphisms to local section lifts and back; this generic sheaf tool is not supplied by the universal-datum unit.
The arbitrary disjoint-cover gluing theorem supplies existence and uniqueness of sections on the refinement; it is a generic sheaf tool.
Left exactness holds for every scheme morphism and is the generic half of exactness, not a replacement for the integral geometric argument.
Enough injectives supplies the hypotheses of the resolution definition of higher direct images.
Generic homological algebra converts established exactness into vanishing of higher derived functors.
Generic localization of an exact functor supplies the termwise derived functor.
The generic cohomology comparison ensures the induced functor preserves bounded below objects.
Generic universal-property identification with the right derived functor supplies the canonical bounded-below comparison.
